description: An FPTAS (*fully polynomial-time approximation scheme*) gives an answer within a factor `1 + ε` of the optimum, in time polynomial in the input size and in `1 / ε`. This one solves the constrained shortest path: the lowest first cost among paths whose second cost is within a budget. It runs `n − 1` Bellman-Ford rounds over the `n` reachable states, and each state keeps at most one path per box of first costs: the one with the smallest second cost. The boxes grow by the factor `1 + ε / (2 (n − 1))`, so the path it returns fits the budget and has a first cost at most `1 + ε` times the optimum (`ε` is capped at 2, and `ε = 0` is exact). Use it when exact search keeps too many labels, because the number of labels here stays polynomial.

papers.title: Approximation of Pareto Optima in Multiple-Objective, Shortest-Path Problems
Multiobjective Optimization: Improved FPTAS for Shortest Paths and Non-Linear Objectives with Applications

papers.authors: José Craveirinha, João Clímaco, Rita Girão-Silva, Marta Pascoal
